title: CT 18: English Language (Correct Usage Of Words)

questions.text:
Evaluate the following word, accompanied by three sentences containing it. Determine the sentence(s) that accurately convey the meaning of the given word.

Assuage

A. To assuage his guilt over forgetting his mother’s birthday, he bought her a massive bouquet of her favorite flowers.

B. The hot sun served to assuage the ice cube, causing it to freeze solid within a matter of seconds.

C. She tried to assuage her intense anger by screaming loudly at her colleagues and slamming her office door.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Only A .

Key Points

  • The word "assuage" means to make an unpleasant feeling less intense or to satisfy a desire.
  • In Sentence A, the use of "assuage" is correct because the subject is trying to ease his guilt by giving his mother a bouquet of flowers. This aligns with the meaning of the word.
  • In Sentence B, the word "assuage" is incorrectly used. The context suggests the opposite of what "assuage" means, as the sun would not cause freezing but rather melting.
  • In Sentence C, the word "assuage" is also incorrectly applied. Screaming and slamming doors are not actions that "ease" or "soothe" anger but rather intensify it.

Correct sentence: To assuage his guilt over forgetting his mother’s birthday, he bought her a massive bouquet of her favorite flowers.

Additional Information

  • Examples of correct usage:
    • He tried to assuage his fear of public speaking by practicing in front of a mirror.
    • She brought a warm blanket to assuage the child's discomfort in the cold weather.
  • Synonyms of "assuage": alleviate, soothe, mitigate, relieve.
  • Antonyms of "assuage": aggravate, intensify, worsen.

questions.text:
Directions: Given below is a word, followed by three sentences that consist of that word. Identify the sentence(s) that express(es) the meaning of the word.

DWINDLE

A. The music was dwindling in the background.

B. Her patience started to dwindle as the queue was not moving.

C. The organization has seen its funding dwindle over the past year.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Both B and C.'

Key Points

  • The word 'Dwindle' as a verb means to diminish gradually in size, amount, or strength.
    • In sentence A, the use of the word 'Dwindle' is incorrect. Music can fade, lower, or die down, but 'dwindle' doesn't fit the context naturally.
    • In sentence B, 'Dwindle' is correctly used as it paints a picture of someone's slowly decreasing patience due to the lack of movement in the queue.
    • In sentence C, 'Dwindle' has also been appropriately used to illustrate the process of gradual lessening of the organization's funding over the past year.
Hence, the only possible answer is option 3.

questions.text:
Directions: Given below is a word, followed by three sentences that consist of that word. Identify the sentence(s) that express(es) the meaning of the word.

COLOSSAL

A. They made a colossal error in judgment.

B. The dinner will be colossal at seven o'clock.

C. The palace's colossal pillars amazed the tourists.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Both A and C.'

Key Points

  • The word 'Colossal' as an adjective means extremely large or great.
    • In sentence A, the word 'Colossal' is used correctly to exaggerate the error in judgement as being huge or great.
    • In sentence B, the use of the word 'Colossal' does not fit the context. It does not make sense to describe a dinner time as 'colossal.'
    • In sentence C, 'Colossal' has appropriately been used to describe the large and impressive pillars of the palace.
Hence, the only possible answer is option 3

questions.text:
Directions: Given below is a word, followed by three sentences that consist of that word. Identify the sentence(s) that express(es) the meaning of the word.

CLAUSTROPHOBIA

A. Being stuck in a crowded elevator triggered her claustrophobia.

B. She was so excited to feel the claustrophobia of the calm lake.

C. Those with claustrophobia avoid small, enclosed spaces when possible.

options.text: All of them

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Both A and C.'


Key Points

  • The word 'Claustrophobia' as a noun means an extreme or irrational fear of confined places.
    • In sentence A, the use of 'Claustrophobia' is correct as it pertains to a claustrophobic episode triggered by a confined space (a crowded elevator).
    • In sentence B, the use of 'Claustrophobia' is incorrect. Calm lakes do not evoke or engender feelings of claustrophobia, nor can a person 'feel' claustrophobia of a calm lake.
    • In sentence C, 'Claustrophobia' is used correctly to describe individuals who avoid small, enclosed spaces due to claustrophobia.
Hence, the only possible answer is option 3.

questions.text:
Direction: Evaluate the following word, accompanied by three sentences containing it. Determine the sentence(s) that accurately convey the meaning of the given word.

Concede

A. The defense team decided to concede the game after losing four key players to injuries.

B. The company had to concede defeat in the marketplace due to intense competition.

C. He would not concede his seat on the bus, despite the glaring need of the elderly woman standing before him.

options.text: Only A
Both A & B
Only C
All A, B & C
None of these

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 2.

Key Points

  • Concede means to admit something is true or valid after first denying it, or to surrender or yield (स्वीकार करना या हार मान लेना).
  • Sentences A and B use "concede" to indicate admitting defeat or acknowledging a difficult situation.
  • Sentence C incorrectly uses "concede"; the character refuses to give up their seat, not yielding or admitting something.
  • Hence, the correct sentences are Both A & B.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Both A & B".

 Additional Information

  • The use of concede involves admitting or yielding in various contexts.

questions.text:
Direction: Evaluate the following word, accompanied by three sentences containing it. Determine the sentence(s) that accurately convey the meaning of the given word.

Abjuration

A. The political leader's abjuration of his earlier views caused a stir among his supporters.

B. She made an abjuration to avoid sweets in order to improve her health.

C. His abjuration from the team was unexpected and left the members in shock.

options.text: Only A
Both A & B
Only C
All A, B & C
None of these

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is: Option 4.

Key Points

  • The word "Abjuration" means the act of renouncing or rejecting something, especially a belief, claim, or oath. (शपथपूर्वक त्याग)
    • Example: The abjuration of the throne by the king led to a period of political instability in the kingdom.
  • In sentence A, the political leader's abjuration of his earlier views implies he formally rejected beliefs he previously held, which aligns with the meaning of abjuration. (शपथपूर्वक त्याग)
    • Example: After years of promoting a strict policy, the politician's abjuration of those views surprised many.
  • In sentence B, making an abjuration to avoid sweets for health reasons can be seen as a personal vow or pledge, somewhat fitting the broader context of abjuration as renunciation. (शपथपूर्वक त्याग)
    • Example: Her abjuration of sugar was a significant step towards a healthier lifestyle.
  • In sentence C, his abjuration from the team, though not a perfect fit due to the phrasing, could be interpreted as a formal renunciation or leaving, which loosely fits the concept of abjuration. (शपथपूर्वक त्याग)
    • Example: The athlete's abjuration from professional sports marked the end of an era.
  • Hence, we can infer that the sentences collectively convey the essence of 'abjuration' through different contexts.

Therefore, the correct answer is: All A, B & C.

questions.text:
Evaluate the following word, accompanied by three sentences containing it. Determine the sentence(s) that accurately convey the meaning of the given word.

Garrulous

A. The detective encountered a garrulous suspect who refused to open his mouth or utter a sound during the entire interrogation. 

B. The garrulous neighbor talked continuously for forty minutes about her garden, barely letting me say a single word.

C. This book features a highly garrulous index, containing only two pages of text and no descriptive explanations.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Only B .

Key Points

  • The word garrulous means excessively talkative, especially about trivial matters.
  • Let us evaluate the sentences:
    • Sentence A: The garrulous suspect who "refused to open his mouth" is contradictory. A garrulous person would talk excessively, not remain silent. Hence, this sentence is incorrect.
    • Sentence B: The neighbor who "talked continuously for forty minutes" clearly demonstrates the meaning of garrulous, which is excessive talking. This sentence is correct.
    • Sentence C: The phrase "a highly garrulous index" is nonsensical, as an index cannot talk. This sentence is incorrect.

Correct sentence: The garrulous neighbor talked continuously for forty minutes about her garden, barely letting me say a single word.

Additional Information

  • Examples of usage:
    • Correct: The garrulous tour guide kept talking about every single tree in the park.
    • Incorrect: The garrulous child sat in complete silence during the lecture.
  • Synonyms: Talkative, loquacious, verbose.
  • Antonyms: Quiet, reserved, taciturn.

questions.text:
Directions: Given below is a word, followed by three sentences that consist of that word. Identify the sentence(s) that express(es) the meaning of the word.

E-COMMERCE

A. She purchased the dress from an e-commerce website.

B. His e-commerce wasn't very good at maths.

C. The little e-commerce in the corner was crying for its mother.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Only A.'

Key Points

  • 'E-commerce' refers to commercial transactions conducted electronically on the internet.
    • In sentence A, 'E-commerce' has been correctly used to refer to online shopping.
    • In sentences B and C, 'E-commerce' is inappropriately used as the context of a person's math skill or a crying entity does not relate to commercial transactions on the internet.

Hence, the only possible answer is option 1.

questions.text:
Directions: Given below is a word, followed by three sentences that consist of that word. Identify the sentence(s) that express(es) the meaning of the word.

VIRTUAL

A. She attended all the meetings in a virtual format.

B. They went virtual shopping over the weekend.

C. She loves the virtual taste of the new dish.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Both A and B.'

Key Points

  • 'Virtual' in the context of technology refers to something that is made, done, seen, etc. on the internet or on a computer rather than in the real world.
    • In sentence A and B, 'Virtual' has been correctly used to refer to attending meetings and shopping on the internet.
    • Sentence C inappropriately uses 'Virtual' as the context does not relate to the term's technological usage pertaining to taste.
Hence, the only possible answer is option 2.

questions.text:
Directions: Given below is a word, followed by three sentences that consist of that word. Identify the sentence(s) that express(es) the meaning of the word.

QUANTIFY

A. She tried to quantify her feelings for him.

B. They quantified their bags before their trip.

C. It's difficult to quantify the impact of the new policy on small businesses.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Both A and C.'

Key Points

  • The word 'Quantify' as a verb means to express or measure the quantity of something.
    • In sentence A, the word 'Quantify' has been correctly used as a verb. Although quantifying feelings may seem abstract, it is a possible usage - she tried to measure or put into numbers her feelings for him.
    • In sentence B, the word 'Quantify' is inappropriately used. It does not make sense to quantify (measure) bags before a trip.
    • In sentence C, the word 'Quantify' has been correctly used as a verb. It is usual to want to measure or quantify the impact of a new policy on businesses.
Hence, the only possible answer is option 3.
